newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour says no taboos in spending review.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour says no taboos in spending review.

text.p: Chief Secretary to the UK Treasury Alistair Darling on Friday said he would rule nothing out in government's spending review.
"The government will not shrink from the spending review, which is an essential part of our approach (to getting financial stability)," Darling told the BBC in an interview.
"We've got to get stability, and to get stability you've got to get public finances in order, and that is what we're doing," he added.
On Wednesday, Darling announced a year-long review of public spending which he said would ensure the government met its manifesto objectives while staying within its tight spending target.

Darling's views echoed those of health secretary Frank Dobson earlier on Friday. Dobson refused to rule out new charges for patients in Britain's National Health Service. Spending there is undergoing review.
Dobson said NHS finances were in an even worse state than he had imagined while in opposition.
